explanations: terra: Moses is told اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ and water bursts from stone; striking stone releases water here, rather than the runner's fire-spark.
terra: فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ redirects the source dictionary's sabq, proof of a horse's excellence, into human competition for good deeds.

luna: The section says the source's dictionary form شَدّ names the horse's run while the human is “shadīd” in love of wealth; “أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ” redirects that intensity of love toward God. | terra: Believers are أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِّلَّهِ, reversing the human who is shadid in love of property by directing the same intensity toward God.

luna: The section shows love of wealth as the human counterpart to a horse's service; this verse's righteous person gives “الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ,” turning attachment into care for others. | terra: وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ makes loved wealth something the righteous give, rather than the terminus of the human's intense attachment.

luna: The section notes that “al-khayr” can mean wealth in its line about love; here “خَيْرًا” is what someone leaves as an estate, a concrete Qur'anic use of that dictionary sense. | terra: إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا uses khayr for property left at death, confirming the wealth sense that underlies the human's حُبِّ الْخَيْرِ in the section.

luna: The section says the horse is both a running animal and a beloved possession; this list places “الْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ” among what people desire and love, making that double role explicit. | terra: الْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ places horses inside the decorated human love of desires and stored wealth, directly supporting the section's two faces of the horse as runner and loved property.

luna: After 3:14 names horses among desired possessions, this verse asks about “better than that” and offers gardens and God's approval, giving the list's own stated alternative to attachment to display and wealth. | terra: Immediately after decorated desires including horses, the ayah asks whether it should announce what is better and locates the enduring reward عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ.

luna: The section's human chest is where concealed contents are sifted; this verse says what people hide or disclose within themselves is known to God, a direct parallel to that inward disclosure. | terra: Whether people hide what is in their breasts or disclose it, God knows it; this directly parallels the section's chest as a temporary container whose contents will be brought out.

luna: Against the section's human clinging to wealth, this verse makes giving from what one loves a condition of reaching righteousness: “مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ.” | terra: لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ turns attachment to valued property into its relinquishment for righteousness.
terra: The ayah contrasts the believers' love with concealed hatred and closes with God's knowledge of breasts, making the chest the place where an outward relationship's contrary truth resides.
luna: After 3:14 lists the loved horses and other desires, this verse says “وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ,” offering a specific opposite direction for human urgency.
luna: Following 3:133's call to hasten toward forgiveness, this verse describes those who spend in ease and hardship; it gives a concrete alternative to the section's human attachment to wealth.

luna: The section's image turns from the horse's winning chest to what is sifted from human chests; this verse says God tests “مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ” and purifies what is in hearts. | terra: In a battle setting, God tests what is in the breasts and purifies what is in the hearts; this directly answers the section's human chest whose contents will be sorted after the charge.
terra: يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ again locates jamʿ in an actual battle encounter, rather than only in the source dictionary's secondary sense of gathering the horse's run.
terra: إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ describes people massed against the believers; faith grows before a threatening gathered force of the kind entered in 100:5.
terra: كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ commands precisely the self-opposing witness that the section reads in the human's testimony against himself.
terra: The remembered covenant and وَقُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا are followed by God's knowledge of breasts, joining pledged service to the inward reality that will test it.
terra: فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ again turns speed and precedence toward good, opposing the human whose intense drive terminates in loved wealth.
terra: أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَدَاوَةً brings together sh-d-d and ʿ-d-w—the two source roots glossed as the horse's run—but in the human sense of most intense enmity.
terra: The breast opened to submission is opposed to a breast made constricted and tight; the human chest carries guidance or refusal, unlike the horse's chest whose exertion is outwardly evident.
terra: وَشَهِدُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ makes the human beings' own testimony establish their unbelief, matching the section's reading of testimony against one's own ingratitude.
terra: شَهِدُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَافِرِينَ gives the same self-incriminating witness that contrasts with the horse's run witnessing in its favor.
terra: أَنِ اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ again makes a struck stone yield springs, a concrete elemental reversal of hooves striking sparks.
terra: يَعْدُونَ فِي السَّبْتِ uses ʿ-d-w for crossing the Lord's limit; the root that names the animal's fastest run becomes human transgression.
terra: أَنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ repeats the warning that valued possessions test the human's relation to God.
terra: يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ names the battlefield meeting of two gathered forces, giving concrete military context to the jamʿ reached by the charge.
terra: Within a battle encounter, the enemy is shown as few and God is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ; the gathered-force setting and inward knowledge meet two distinct details of the section.

luna: The section stages horses rushing into a group; this verse names “رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ” prepared as military force, giving the mounted-charge scene its place in deliberate preparation and deterrence. | terra: رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ presents horses held ready as concentrated power for a collective purpose, matching the trained animal that gathers its whole run for its owner's work.
terra: شَاهِدِينَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ بِالْكُفْرِ sets testimony explicitly against the witnesses themselves, the human side of the section's horse-human reversal.

luna: The section places a horse and love of wealth beside “my Lord”; this verse marks the boundary where beloved wealth, trade, and homes are dearer than God, His Messenger, and striving in His cause. | terra: The ayah sets possessions, profitable trade, and pleasing homes against love of God, His Messenger, and striving, defining the loyalty at stake in the section's love-of-khayr comparison.
terra: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way enact the section's misdirected love of property and prepare the bodily fire scene in 9:35.

terra: Hoarded wealth is heated in hellfire and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs; the ayah specifically joins property, fire, and the body, images the section holds together around the horse-human comparison.
terra: أَلَا حِينَ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ describes an attempted inward concealment and says God knows what is hidden, clarifying why the human chest cannot remain closed.
terra: إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ is a literal human race; it plausibly makes physical the horse-human transfer of sabq, but its narrative purpose is the brothers' alibi rather than moral striving.
terra: God subjects ships to run by His command for human benefit, beginning the service catalogue that culminates in the ungrateful human of 14:34.
terra: The sun and moon are دَائِبَيْنِ, ceaselessly performing their appointed motion for humans; their sustained service adds a cosmic analogue to the horse's total exertion.

luna: The section opposes the horse's service to its owner with the human's ingratitude to the Lord; this verse places innumerable divine favors beside the human being “ظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ,” making ingratitude a response to provision. | terra: After a catalogue of powers placed in human service, إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ makes the same turn from devoted provision to the ungrateful human.

luna: The section follows horses moving at dawn; this verse notices livestock's beauty both when brought home and when sent out, giving the animal's daily departure and return a valued human-facing scene.

luna: The section's source gloss for الإنسان places the rider beside the animal; this verse says livestock carry people's heavy loads to places they could not reach without difficulty, making the mount's service concrete. | terra: Livestock carry burdens to a land people could reach only with severe bodily effort; beside the horses of 16:8, it makes an animal's expenditure of body for its owner explicit.

luna: The section links the human to the animal's rider-facing side and treats the horse as cherished property; this verse explicitly gives “الْخَيْلَ” for riding and adornment, joining service to display. | terra: Horses are made لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً, coupling the rider-facing body developed from insiyy with the horse as an object of adornment and desire.

luna: The section names horse legs and necks in the Solomon passage, then contrasts the animal with accountable humans; this verse places each person's record around his neck and says it will be brought out open on the resurrection day. | terra: Every human's record is fastened to him and brought out as an open book; it supplies the personal evidence that allows 17:14 to make the human his own accountant.

luna: For the section's human who is himself witness to his conduct, this verse says “كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا,” making the person his own reckoner. | terra: كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا makes the person sufficient evidence for his own reckoning, a non-witness-root parallel to self-testimony in the section.

luna: The section's horse expends its run for an owner; Satan is told to rally “بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ,” a specific reversal in which mounted force serves a misleading cause. | terra: وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ stages cavalry and infantry brought against people; it is the Quran's other compact scene of horse-borne assault amid a force.
terra: The Lord makes ships run for humans so that they seek His bounty; this vehicle's commanded service supplies a close non-animal parallel to the mount spent in its owner's work.
terra: After the carrying vessel has saved them, the humans turn away and وَكَانَ الْإِنسَانُ كَفُورًا; the service-to-ingratitude sequence directly matches the section.
terra: وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ uses the source's ʿ-d-w root for the eyes passing beyond people toward زِينَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا, redirecting the runner-root away from worldly adornment.

luna: The section treats horses as both valued possessions and working bodies; this verse calls wealth and children adornment of worldly life and contrasts them with enduring righteous deeds, clarifying what the horse's visible value cannot secure. | terra: الْمَالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا names property as worldly adornment, then prefers enduring righteous deeds; it supplies the boundary for the decorated horses and wealth of 3:14.

luna: The section turns from the horse's witnessed performance to human accountability; this verse lays out the record and says it omits neither small nor large deeds, making the person's conduct an inspectable account.

terra: آنَسْتُ نَارًا uses the named hamza-nun-sin root in the different sense of perceiving fire; it meets both the source's rider-facing insiyy and the charge's sparks without replacing either sense.

luna: The section's dictionary form describes a racehorse made lean like an arrow-shaft; this verse also pictures a lean mount, a camel coming from distant passes for pilgrimage, though its leanness reflects travel rather than the horse's training. | terra: كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ is a lean mount arriving from a distant pass; it concretizes the source dictionary's damura, the trained horse pared down until it resembles an arrow shaft.
terra: Sacrificial camels are سَخَّرْنَاهَا لَكُمْ and humans are told to mention God over them, joining a subjected animal body to acknowledgement of its true giver.
terra: Neither flesh nor blood reaches God, but human taqwa does; this distinguishes the animal's offered body from the inward human quality sought by the Lord.
terra: The ayah says blindness belongs to الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ; where the horse's chest visibly wins, the human chest houses an unseen moral failure.
terra: After God gives life, death, and life again, إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ ties human ingratitude to the Lord who controls his whole course and return.
terra: Cattle provide drink, many benefits, and food; this repeated animal-to-human service enlarges the contrast with the human who withholds gratitude from his own provider.
terra: وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ places the human physically upon the carrying animal, corresponding to the source dictionary's rider-facing side.
terra: يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ combines haste and precedence in good works, the ethical counterpart of the horse's excellent, outstripping run.

luna: The section sets the horse's bodily performance as its evidence against the human's self-witness; here “أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم” bear witness to what people did. | terra: Tongues, hands, and feet تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ with what they did; a body's own action becomes evidence, as the horse's running body proves its quality and the human body indicts its owner.
terra: The lamp's oil nearly gives light وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ; fire almost appearing without contact forms a precise boundary against the runner's contact-made sparks.

luna: Against the section's human whose love of wealth is fierce, this verse describes people whom trade does not distract from God's remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving, while they fear the day hearts and eyes turn about. | terra: لَا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلَا بَيْعٌ عَن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ supplies the faithful side of the ambiguity in Solomon's love of horses in relation to remembrance of his Lord.
terra: إِنِّي آنَسْتُ نَارًا repeats the hamza-nun-sin/fire conjunction and adds a sought burning brand, a specific secondary meeting of the section's insan-root and ignition image.
terra: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ states the Lord's knowledge of what breasts conceal, the hidden content later brought out in the section.
terra: آنَسَ مِن جَانِبِ الطُّورِ نَارًا again uses the named root for perceiving fire on a journey; the explicit side, journey, and fire make the secondary echo especially concrete.
terra: وَرَبُّكَ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ repeats the conceal/reveal pair under the Lord's knowledge, strengthening the chest's role as temporary enclosure rather than refuge.

terra: أَوَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِمَا فِي صُدُورِ الْعَالَمِينَ challenges a public claim of faith by the inward content God knows, matching the section's move from outward human stance to inner evidence.
terra: إِنَّ أَنكَرَ الْأَصْوَاتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ names an animal's own cry, sharpening the section's express boundary: ḍabḥ is exerted breath, neither neigh nor other call.
terra: Return to God, disclosure of deeds, and عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ connect the chest's hidden contents to the final accounting that follows the horse scene.
terra: إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ places the breast's contents within God's wider knowledge of every hidden thing.
terra: لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِي لَهَا أَن تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ sets a boundary on overtaking within ordered motion; it only indirectly illuminates the racehorse whose excellence is proved by overtaking.

luna: The section makes a runner's own body attest to its performance; here mouths are sealed while “أَيْدِيهِمْ” speak and “أَرْجُلُهُم” testify against people. | terra: Hands speak and feet تَشْهَدُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ, making the very limbs that carried human action bear adverse witness.

luna: The section says the animal gives its body to its owner's work; this passage begins by saying livestock were created for people and “فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ,” grounding that service in divine provision. | terra: Humans are made owners of livestock created by God, فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ, establishing the lower owner-animal relation against which the section measures the human-Lord relation.

luna: Following 36:71's livestock belonging to people, this verse says they were subdued and some are mounts; it supplies the bodily service that the section sets against human ingratitude. | terra: وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ and فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ show the animal's body subjected for human riding, the same bodily service the section hears in breath and sees in legs.

luna: After 36:71–72 name livestock, their subjection, and riding, this verse names their benefits and asks “أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ”; gratitude is the explicit opposite of the human's كَنُود. | terra: After the animals' benefits, أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ exposes the missing gratitude; it is the exact moral turn made when the devoted horse is followed by the kanud human.
terra: Fire is produced from a green tree, فَإِذَا أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ; like sparks struck from the runner's contact with stone, an apparently contrary material releases fire.

luna: The section explicitly compares its action-named oath to this opening, “الصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا”; this verse contributes the first role in the same compact oath by an active feminine plural group. | terra: وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا is the section's stated parallel: an oath introduces a feminine plural known by its action rather than a supplied name.

luna: In the oath form the section identifies, “فَالزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْرًا” adds a next, forceful action after the ranks, paralleling the linked stages of the horse charge without equating their actors. | terra: فَالزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْرًا adds the next action with fa, directly paralleling the running, striking, raising, and entering stages chained in surah 100.
terra: فَالتَّالِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا completes the action-defined oath sequence begun in 37:1; its own contribution is the third immediately linked act.

luna: This verse immediately precedes the horse display in 38:31 and calls Solomon “نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ” who repeatedly turned back to God; it frames, without deciding, the following horse-and-remembrance statement. | terra: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ establishes Solomon as an excellent, returning servant before the horses appear, materially informing the two possible relations between horse-love and remembrance of his Lord.

luna: The section's action-known horse reappears explicitly in the evening display of “الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ”; the horses here are poised and presented, extending the image from exertion to valued form. | terra: The noble, swift horses, الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ, are the Quran's explicit presentation of the animal inferred in 100:1 from breath, stride, and speed.

luna: The section directly connects its “love of good/wealth” wording to this horse scene: “حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي” joins horses, intense love, and remembrance of the Lord, while the section preserves both readings of عَنْ. | terra: Solomon's حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ joins love of valuable horses to ذِكْرِ رَبِّي; the section explicitly sets this beside the human's love of khayr and ingratitude to his Lord.

luna: 38:31–32 establish the displayed horses and Solomon's ambiguous words about love and remembrance; this verse itself returns the horses and names “السُّوقِ وَالْأَعْنَاقِ,” keeping the bodily horse scene present without resolving the ambiguity. | terra: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ returns the horses of 38:31-32, and touching their legs and necks makes their trained body—the section's legs, narrowed frame, and service to an owner—visible.
terra: This ayah joins kufr versus gratitude, return to your Lord, and إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ; it gathers the section's human ingratitude and exposed chest into one statement.
terra: A breast opened to submission and light from its Lord is set against hardened hearts, specifying the inward human condition hidden within the ṣadr.

luna: The section contrasts the horse's chest that wins visibly with the human chest whose contents are brought out; this verse says God knows “مَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ,” naming what the judgment discloses. | terra: يَعْلَمُ ... وَمَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ states that what breasts hide is already known, corresponding directly to the later extraction of their contents.

luna: The section's rider-facing horse and animal service find a direct parallel in this verse's statement that God made livestock for people to ride and eat from, locating the mount within divine provision. | terra: God makes cattle so that some are ridden and some eaten, another direct instance of an animal body fitted to human use.

luna: The section contrasts a horse's chest with what is brought out of human chests; this verse says mounts carry people to a need “فِي صُدُورِكُمْ,” joining the rider's bodily transport to the same chest-word in a different, outward-directed sense. | terra: Humans obtain needs through livestock and are carried on them and ships; the ayah develops the total service that the section attributes to the trained horse.

luna: The section's horse is witnessed through its bodily action, while the human is answerable for his own; here hearing, sight, and skin bear witness against the people themselves. | terra: Hearing, sight, and skins شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ, sharply developing the section's contrast between a horse's bodily performance testifying for it and the human body testifying against him.

luna: 41:20 has just named hearing, sight, and skin as witnesses; this verse's own question to their skins makes bodily testimony answerable, paralleling the section's body-as-evidence image. | terra: The condemned ask their skins لِمَ شَهِدتُّمْ عَلَيْنَا; this row contributes the explicit recognition that one's own body has become an adverse witness.

luna: After 41:20–21 make the body testify, this verse says people did not hide from those witnesses but thought God did not know much of their deeds, a direct boundary against the Lord's knowledge in 100:11. | terra: The sinners could not hide from their own hearing, sight, and skins testifying; the ayah explains the failed concealment implied by the bodily witnesses in 41:20-21.

luna: After 41:22 names the thought that God did not know their deeds, this verse calls that very assumption ruinous, giving consequence to the hidden conduct and divine knowledge in the section's closing judgment.

terra: لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنسَانُ مِن دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ joins al-insan to an untiring appetite for khayr; the sense is broader than wealth, but the persistence sharpens the section's diagnosis of attachment.
terra: After truth is established and falsehood erased, إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ makes the inward content part of what cannot survive concealed or falsified.

luna: The section's horse is the animal under a rider; this verse says God made livestock and ships among what people ride, setting that mounted relation within provision from the Lord. | terra: Ships and cattle are made as مَا تَرْكَبُونَ; the mount-human relation supplies the concrete setting for the source dictionary's animal side nearest the rider.

luna: The preceding 43:12 establishes the mount; this verse's own “عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ” turns riding into remembrance of the Lord's favor, the response set against 100:6's ingratitude. | terra: The rider settles on the mount's back and must remember the Lord's favor, turning the section's horse-and-owner relation into a demand that the human acknowledge his own Lord.

luna: After 43:12–13 name the mount and remembrance of its favor, this verse completes the rider's words with “إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ,” returning the scene to the Lord. | terra: وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ places return to the Lord in the rider's mouth, answering the section's human who is attached to property yet will be exposed before his Lord.
terra: Immediately after the mount and remembrance scene, إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ states the same human ingratitude that follows the running animal in surah 100.
luna: The section asks the reader to picture what is brought out of the chest; this verse asks whether God will not bring out “أَضْغَانَهُمْ,” naming concealed resentment as inward content.

luna: The section puts a human on a horse and makes the horse's performance its witness; this verse brings each soul with a driver and a witness. The passage does not say the driver is mounted, so the connection is the role arrangement at judgment rather than a repeated horse scene. | terra: Every soul arrives مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ; driver and witness surround the judged human, echoing the section's rider relation and its transformed witness language.

luna: The section reads 100:1–5 as a linked oath sequence; “وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا” begins another oath by an active feminine plural group, contributing its first staged role. | terra: وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا opens another oath with an unnamed feminine plural discerned by an energetic action.

luna: In that separate oath sequence, “فَالْحَامِلَاتِ وِقْرًا” supplies a next role joined by ف, matching the section's movement from one action to another. | terra: فَالْحَامِلَاتِ وِقْرًا turns immediately by fa from scattering to bearing, closely matching the section's reading of chained stages as one developing movement.

luna: “فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا” names smooth running in the same linked oath sequence, a direct movement parallel to the section's fast-running animal. | terra: فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا contributes literal running or coursing inside the action-defined oath chain, a direct counterpart to the runners of 100:1.

luna: “فَالْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْرًا” completes this oath's sequence with an assigned act; like 100:1–5, the verse participates in an oath built from successive doers. | terra: فَالْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْرًا gives the chain's next assigned act, reinforcing how the subjects are disclosed by their ordered work.

luna: The section distinguishes the horse's own performance as witness from the human's ingratitude; this verse says the human has only what he strives for, keeping effort and its account attached to the doer.
terra: أَمْ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ voices a gathered host's confidence; 54:45 then supplies that jamʿ's defeat, paralleling the force entered in 100:5.
terra: سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ gives the battlefield fate of a gathered force, the same kind of jamʿ into whose middle the surah-100 runners plunge.
terra: وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ transfers distinction through precedence from the well-bred racer to the foremost human beings before God.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ uses the same ignition verb heard in 100:2, moving from hoof-made sparks to the fire humans kindle.
terra: وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ repeats the direct formulation that the contents of human breasts are already known before their final extraction.

luna: The section makes the horse both a beautiful working body and a coveted possession; this verse calls worldly life adornment and names boasting and competition in wealth, then shows that growth withering away. | terra: Worldly life is adornment, boasting, and rivalry in wealth before it withers; this reverses the apparent durability promised by intense love of valuable property.

luna: The section's animal races into a crowd while the human clings to wealth; “سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ” redirects racing toward forgiveness from the Lord. | terra: سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ commands humans to race toward forgiveness, redirecting the section's bodily race toward the proper human goal.

luna: The section stages horses rushing into a gathered force; this verse says no horses or camels were spurred in the acquisition it describes, marking a specific boundary where gain came without the mounted charge. | terra: فَمَا أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ makes the absence of spurred horses legally decisive; it is a precise boundary around the fastest horse-run that animates the section.
terra: عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ uses the runner-root in the human enemy sense while warning against offering affection to enemies of the Lord, joining the section's root echo to misdirected attachment.

luna: The section sets the human's love of wealth against remembrance of the Lord; this verse gathers people for Friday prayer and commands them to hasten to God's remembrance and leave trade. | terra: فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ commands movement toward remembrance and away from trade, a direct ethical reorientation of both running and property-love.
luna: After 62:9 gathers worshippers away from trade, this verse sends them back into the land to seek God's bounty while remembering Him, showing movement and livelihood kept under remembrance.

luna: Following 62:9–10's prayer and return to work, this verse says people disperse toward trade or amusement and leave the Messenger standing; its own contribution is a crowd's movement toward worldly gain over the Lord's message. | terra: When people see trade or amusement they disperse toward it and leave the messenger standing; bodily movement toward gain realizes the danger opened by Solomon's horse-love in relation to remembrance.
terra: لَا تُلْهِكُمْ أَمْوَالُكُمْ ... عَن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ gives the explicit boundary between loved property and remembrance that the section opens through 38:32.

luna: The section ends with the Lord fully aware of people on the day their inward contents are exposed; this verse expressly joins what people conceal and reveal with God's knowledge of “ذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ.” | terra: God knows what humans hide and reveal and is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ, directly corresponding to the section's sorting of what lies within chests.
terra: Some spouses and children are عَدُوًّا لَّكُمْ; the runner-root's enemy sense appears inside the very attachments that can compete with loyalty to the Lord.
terra: إِنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ identifies possessions and family as a test, clarifying why intense love of khayr is morally diagnostic.

luna: The section ends with what is brought out of the chest and the Lord's full knowledge; this verse says God knows “ذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ” whether speech is hidden or voiced. | terra: Whether speech is concealed or voiced, إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ; inwardness does not shield the human from the Lord's knowledge.

luna: The section's dictionary branch for جَمْعًا describes a horse gathering its run in one charge; “جَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ” instead describes a person collecting and hoarding, turning gathered force into possession. | terra: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَى depicts a human gathering and hoarding, another pointed redirection of the horse's collected motion into possessiveness.
terra: وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا uses khayr for what the human receives and withholds, a specific character parallel to the possessiveness heard in love of khayr.

luna: The section's horse races into a crowd before the surah turns to graves; here people emerge from graves rushing as if toward standing stones, reversing the scene into a human rush whose destination is exposed at judgment.
terra: أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ moves jamʿ from the horse collecting its living run to God's reassembling the human body for judgment.

luna: The section says the human is witness to his own ingratitude, unlike the horse whose performance attests to its quality; “بَصِيرَةٌ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ” makes the self the witness despite excuses. | terra: بَلِ الْإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ is the clearest nonlexical parallel to the human being evidence against himself in 100:7.
terra: وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ says excuses cannot displace the self-knowledge stated in 75:14, clarifying the force of the human's adverse testimony.

luna: The section explicitly cites “الْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا” as an action-led oath; this verse establishes a group named by what it does, like the successive doers in 100:1–5. | terra: وَالْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا is the section's second stated parallel, an oath by a feminine plural identified through what it does.

luna: The section explicitly cites the following “فَالْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفًا”; this verse supplies a forceful next movement joined by ف, matching the section's linked oath stages. | terra: فَالْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفًا makes a following burst of force with fa, directly corresponding to the section's uninterrupted acceleration from one act to the next.

luna: The section's cited oath continues in this verse with “وَالنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْرًا”; its own contribution is another action-named collective in the staged sequence. | terra: وَالنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْرًا continues the same unnamed collective through another staged action; it extends the sequence named by 77:1-2.

luna: “فَالْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقًا” adds a further act to the oath sequence the section compares with 100:1–5, joined by the same stepwise ف. | terra: فَالْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقًا supplies a further fa-linked act, showing how an oath can define agents cumulatively through successive effects.

luna: “فَالْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا” is the next active role in the sequence; it extends the action-led oath form that the section uses to read the horse's successive movements. | terra: فَالْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا completes the continuing chain with what the agents deliver, as each surah-100 participle adds a new consequence of motion.

luna: The identity of this oath's actors is debated; on its wording, “وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا” opens another sequence of feminine plural action-titles, matching the section's action-named oath group. | terra: وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا begins an oath series of feminine plurals whose identities are carried by strenuous acts, like the horse disclosed by exertion.

luna: This verse adds “وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا” to that active feminine-plural oath sequence, paralleling the section's way of identifying a collective by its movement. | terra: وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا adds another bodily force to the unnamed group sequence and prepares the transition into rapid movement.

luna: “وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا” names a moving group within the oath sequence, a motion-stage parallel to the section's linked run and charge. | terra: وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا makes flowing motion itself the group's designation, parallel to recognizing the animal solely from its gait.

luna: The section's horse runs ahead and its chest wins the race; “فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا” gives a direct race-ahead role inside another staged oath sequence. | terra: فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا joins fa-linked acceleration to overtaking; the source dictionary likewise calls the horse's run a witness to its sabq.

luna: “فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا” completes the sequence of active oath-titles; the section's point is likewise that successive roles, not an animal's name, carry the opening image. | terra: فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا completes the movement with purposeful execution, matching the section's emphasis that accumulated speed is given to a task.
terra: قُتِلَ الْإِنسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ gives the same stark judgment of the human's ingratitude toward his maker, though without the horse comparison.
luna: The section ends its human contrast with what is brought out from within; “وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ” gives a neighboring judgment scene in which the records themselves are opened.
terra: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ opens an oath by entities identified through retreating motion, another close instance of the section's unnamed oath-subjects disclosed by what they do.
terra: الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ identifies the oath-subjects as coursing and disappearing; their running both echoes the 100:1 runners and meets the horses hidden behind the veil in 38:32.
terra: وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ makes dawn breathe inside an oath; it strikingly joins the section's audible breath to the morning reached by the running sequence.
luna: Surah 100:9 and this verse share “بُعْثِرَ” with the graves: the horse image's human turn ends at what comes out of burial, and this verse states that overturning directly.
luna: 82:4 has just overturned the graves, paralleling 100:9; this verse adds that every soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind, completing the disclosure of deeds.

terra: The sky أَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ listens to its Lord as it undergoes its assigned act, the creation-level counterpart to the horse giving itself to an owner and the human failing his Lord.
terra: The earth likewise listens to its Lord and is bound to do so, repeating the obedience that throws the section's human ingratitude into relief.

luna: The section makes the horse's hard breathing audible in its run; this verse describes the human as “كَادِحٌ” laboring toward the Lord until meeting Him, shifting exertion from the charge to an inevitable encounter.

luna: The section's inner contents are sifted after burial is undone; “يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ” gives the parallel scene of hidden inward things being exposed. | terra: يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ states without the chest word that inward secrets will be tested, the same disclosure staged in the section's final horse-human contrast.
terra: وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا gives a concrete acquisitive act immediately before the intense love of wealth in 89:20.

luna: The section calls the human intensely attached to “good/wealth”; “وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا” states that attachment as abundant love of wealth. | terra: وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا directly restates the intense human love of property that the section hears in لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ.
terra: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ states that wealth cannot serve its owner at his fall, opposing the animal body that does serve its owner with the property the human trusts.
luna: The section's dust-raising charge gives way to the buried world's disclosure; here “أَثْقَالَهَا” are thrown up by the earth, a concrete companion scene to the graves opened in 100:9.
terra: The earth تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا, so a nonhuman thing reports what occurred through it; this parallels bodily action serving as its own evidence.

luna: The section's dictionary entry uses صَدَرَ الفَرَس for a horse that finishes ahead on its chest; here “يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ” sends people out in scattered groups to see their deeds, turning the chest/race image toward reckoning. | terra: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا uses the named ṣ-d-r root for people issuing forth at judgment, while the source dictionary uses it for a horse arriving first by its chest.
luna: The section notes that “al-khayr” in 100:8 can mean wealth; here “خَيْرًا” is a good deed that its doer will see, contrasting the coveted good/property with good that is actually done.
luna: After 99:7 says a deed of good will be seen, this verse completes the pair with a deed of evil; it extends the section's own-witness motif to both sides of the human account.

luna: The section sets the horse's charge beside human attachment to wealth; “أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ” names abundance-rivalry as a human preoccupation, a specific social counterpart to that attachment. | terra: أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ makes acquisitive increase distract the human, a direct development of the section's intense attachment to property.

luna: After 102:1 names rivalry in abundance, this verse says it lasts “حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ”; it brings the property race to the grave scene that follows the horse image in Surah 100. | terra: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ carries distraction by increase straight to the graves, the same abrupt passage from love of wealth to opened graves in surah 100.

luna: The section's dictionary branch for جَمْعًا says a horse gathers its whole run in one surge; “جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ” uses that root for a person accumulating and counting wealth, reversing concentrated motion into hoarding. | terra: جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ redirects gathering from the source dictionary's horse collecting its run into one thrust to a human collecting and counting wealth.
terra: The wealth-gatherer thinks أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ; this ayah contributes the delusion attached to the gathering named in 104:2.
terra: نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ joins the wealth-gatherer's fate to kindled fire, a specific meeting of the section's property attachment and its ignition image.
terra: الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ carries that fire into human hearts, joining the wealth scene to the section's eventual exposure of what lies inside the chest.
